Build reference¶

This page gives all the CMake settings of wvt, what each setting enables or disables, and the programs that the build makes.

Configure and compile¶

cmake -S . -B build [OPTIONS]
cmake --build build -j

Give each option as -DNAME=VALUE. CMake keeps the values in build/CMakeCache.txt. Thus, when you configure the same build folder again, you do not have to give the options again. To go back to the default of an option, delete build/CMakeCache.txt, or give the default value.

The build script¶

scripts/build.sh does the two steps above for one CPU architecture. It builds in the folder build.<arch> at the top of the source tree, for example build.arm64 or build.x86_64. A sanitizer build goes in build.<arch>.<sanitizer>, for example build.arm64.thread.

scripts/build.sh [options] [-- extra CMake arguments]

Option

Function

-a, --arch ARCH

x86_64 or arm64 (amd64 and aarch64 are also accepted). The default is the architecture of the computer

-t, --type TYPE

Release (default), Debug, RelWithDebInfo or MinSizeRel

-j, --jobs N

The number of parallel compile jobs. The default is the number of CPUs

-B, --build-dir DIR

Use DIR, not build.<arch>

--toolchain FILE

A CMake toolchain file. On Linux, a build for a different architecture needs one

--clean

Delete the build folder first

--test

Run the self-checks (ctest) after the build

-n, --dry-run

Show the commands, but do not run them

--no-rtlsdr, --no-uhd, --no-bb, --no-skiq, --no-audio, --no-cuda, --no-metal

Turn the feature off (WVT_WITH_...=OFF)

--with-rtlsdr, --with-uhd, --with-bb, --with-skiq, --with-audio, --with-cuda, --with-metal

The feature must be in the build. The configure step stops if its library is missing (WVT_WITH_...=ON)

--no-gpu

The same as --no-cuda --no-metal

--minimal

All the features off: the file viewer, the simulator and the signal generator only

--werror, --bb-sim, --fuzz

WVT_WERROR=ON, WVT_BB_SIM=ON, WVT_FUZZ=ON

--sanitize KIND

address or thread (WVT_SANITIZE)

Without a --no- or --with- option, a feature is in the build if its library is found, as in a cmake build without options.

A different architecture:

  • macOS compiles for it directly (CMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES). An x86_64 build runs on Apple silicon with Rosetta. But the Homebrew libraries are for one architecture only, so turn off the features that use them (for example --minimal), or install the libraries for the other architecture.

  • Linux needs a cross compiler and libraries for the other architecture: give them with --toolchain FILE.

Examples:

scripts/build.sh                                   # this computer, all the features that are found
scripts/build.sh --no-cuda --no-uhd --test         # two features off, then the self-checks
scripts/build.sh --arch x86_64 --minimal           # macOS: an Intel build on Apple silicon
scripts/build.sh --sanitize thread --type RelWithDebInfo
scripts/build.sh -- -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=89  # extra CMake arguments

The AUTO, ON and OFF values have the same meaning for all options:

AUTO

CMake builds the function if it finds the necessary library or toolkit. If not, CMake builds wvt without the function and tells you why.

ON

CMake must build the function. If the library or toolkit is missing, the configure step stops with an error.

OFF

CMake does not build the function. CMake does not look for the library.

Use ON in scripts and CI jobs, where a missing library must cause an error.

CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE¶

Sets the compiler optimization. If you do not give a value, wvt uses Release.

  • Release compiles with -O3 -DNDEBUG (the CMake default for GCC and clang). Use this value for normal use. The waterfall and the demodulators are much slower without optimization.

  • Debug compiles with -g and no optimization. Use it with a debugger.

  • RelWithDebInfo compiles with optimization and debug symbols.

X11_ROOT¶

macOS only. Sets the folder of XQuartz. The default is /opt/X11. The build links ${X11_ROOT}/lib/libX11.dylib and ${X11_ROOT}/lib/libGL.dylib, and uses the headers in ${X11_ROOT}/include. If libX11.dylib is not in this folder, the configure step stops.

On Linux, CMake finds X11 and OpenGL with its standard FindX11 and FindOpenGL modules. The build uses the legacy libGL.so, which has the GL and the GLX functions.

WVT_WITH_RTLSDR¶

Enables or disables the RTL-SDR device backend (src/device/sdr_rtlsdr.cpp).

  • CMake finds librtlsdr with pkg-config (the librtlsdr module).

  • CMake also checks for rtlsdr_set_bias_tee(). This function is in librtlsdr builds from 2018 and later. Without it, the bias-tee option is not available.

  • Without this backend, the device list does not show RTL-SDR devices.

Output: wvt: RTL-SDR support enabled (librtlsdr <version>).

WVT_WITH_UHD¶

Enables or disables the USRP backend (src/device/sdr_uhd.cpp). This backend receives and transmits, with all USRPs that UHD supports: the USB B200 family and the network N3xx, X3xx and X4xx.

  • CMake finds UHD with pkg-config (the uhd module). If pkg-config does not find it, CMake uses the UHDConfig.cmake file of UHD.

  • wvt uses the C API of UHD (uhd.h). Thus the build does not need the Boost headers.

  • Without this backend, wvt cannot receive from a USRP, and the signal generator cannot transmit.

Output: wvt: UHD support enabled (UHD <version>).

WVT_WITH_BB¶

Enables or disables the Signal Hound BB60 backend (src/device/sdr_bb60.cpp). It needs bb_api from the Signal Hound SDK. Refer to Live devices.

  • CMake looks for bb_api.h and the library in SIGNALHOUND_SDK_DIR. It uses the library for the CPU of the build: Linux x86-64 (the newest version 5 library), Linux ARM64, or macOS ARM.

  • CMake copies the library into build/bb_api/ under its run-time name. wvt finds it there through its rpath. On Linux x86-64, CMake also copies libftd2xx.so.

  • An x86-64 macOS build cannot use the ARM library. CMake then tells you to configure with -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64.

  • Without this backend, the device list does not show BB60 devices.

Output: wvt: Signal Hound BB60 support enabled (bb_api 5.0.x, <library>).

SIGNALHOUND_SDK_DIR¶

The folder of the extracted Signal Hound SDK, for example $HOME/signal_hound_sdk. A prefix with include/bb_api.h and lib/libbb_api.* also works. If the library is installed in a system folder, such as /usr/local/lib, CMake finds it without this option.

WVT_BB_SIM¶

ON builds the BB60 backend against a simulated BB60D (tools/bb_sim/) instead of the SDK. Use it for CI and tests. The build then also makes bb_check, which tests the backend. Do not use it for normal use: the device list then shows the simulated BB60.

WVT_WITH_SKIQ¶

Enables or disables the Epiq Sidekiq backend (src/device/sdr_skiq.cpp). It needs libsidekiq from the Sidekiq SDK, version 4.14.0 or later. Refer to Live devices.

  • CMake uses the first SDK folder in this list: SIDEKIQ_SDK_DIR, the environment variable SIDEKIQ_SDK_DIR, ~/sidekiq_sdk_current, the newest third_party/sidekiq_sdk/sidekiq_sdk_v*.

  • CMake runs bin/sidekiq-config of the SDK for the version, the include folder and the static link flags. It keeps the link flags in their order. An SDK without sidekiq-config is linked from lib/libsidekiq__<cpu>.a and the support libraries in lib/support/.

  • The SDK is for Linux only. On macOS, the backend is not built.

  • Without this backend, the device list does not show Sidekiq cards.

Output: wvt: Sidekiq support enabled (SDK 4.26.0, <folder>).

SIDEKIQ_SDK_DIR¶

The folder of the extracted Sidekiq SDK: the folder with bin/sidekiq-config and sidekiq_core/inc/sidekiq_api.h, for example $HOME/sidekiq_sdk_v4.26.0.

WVT_SKIQ_SIM¶

ON builds the Sidekiq backend against a simulated card (tools/skiq_sim/) instead of the SDK, also on macOS. Use it for CI and tests. skiq_check then also tests the backend. Do not use it for normal use: the device list then shows the simulated card.

WVT_WITH_AUDIO¶

Enables or disables audio playback through the bundled miniaudio library.

  • On macOS, the build links CoreAudio, AudioToolbox and CoreFoundation.

  • On Linux, the build does not need development packages. At run time, miniaudio loads PipeWire, PulseAudio or ALSA, whichever is available.

  • AUTO and ON have the same result, because the library is in the repository.

  • With OFF, the audio window cannot play sound. The demodulator and the WAV export still work.

Output: wvt: audio playback enabled (miniaudio).

WVT_WITH_CUDA¶

Enables or disables the CUDA GPU backend (src/gpu/gpu_cuda.cu) for NVIDIA GPUs. Refer to GPU processing.

The backend needs all of these conditions:

  • Linux. CUDA is not available on macOS.

  • CMake 3.18 or later.

  • The CUDA toolkit 12.0 or later, with nvcc and cuFFT. For RTX 50-series GPUs, use CUDA 12.8 or later.

If CMake does not find nvcc on the PATH, give its location with -DCMAKE_CUDA_COMPILER=/usr/local/cuda/bin/nvcc.

A CUDA build also runs on a computer without an NVIDIA GPU or driver. wvt then uses the CPU, and the log tells you why.

Output: wvt: CUDA support enabled (CUDA 12.x, archs ..., static cuFFT).

WVT_CUDA_STATIC¶

Sets how the build links the CUDA runtime and cuFFT. Applies only when the CUDA backend builds.

  • ON (default) links the CUDA runtime and cuFFT into the binary. The binary is approximately 270 MB larger. It needs only the NVIDIA driver at run time.

  • OFF links the shared libraries. The binary is small, but the computer that runs it must have the CUDA runtime and cuFFT libraries.

CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES¶

Sets the GPU architectures that the CUDA code is compiled for. Applies only when the CUDA backend builds. If you do not give a value, wvt uses:

CUDA version

Architectures

GPUs

12.0 to 12.7

75-real 80-real 86-real 89-real 90

RTX 20xx to 40xx, A100, H100, plus PTX for newer GPUs

12.8 and later

75-real 80-real 86-real 89-real 90-real 120

The same, plus RTX 50xx

A shorter list makes a smaller binary and a faster build. For example, for an RTX 4090 only, use -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=89. The GPU must have compute capability 7.5 or later.

WVT_WITH_METAL¶

macOS only. Enables or disables the Metal GPU backend (src/gpu/gpu_metal.mm) for Apple GPUs. Refer to GPU processing.

  • The backend needs an Objective-C++ compiler and the Metal and MetalPerformanceShadersGraph frameworks. The Command Line Tools have all of them. You do not need Xcode.

  • The GPU kernels compile when wvt uses the GPU for the first time (approximately 0.2 s).

  • The GPU path needs macOS 14 or later at run time. Older versions use the CPU.

  • On Linux, ON causes an error, and AUTO disables the backend.

Output: wvt: Metal support enabled (MPSGraph FFT; the GPU path needs macOS 14 at run time).

WVT_WERROR¶

ON makes the compiler warnings in the wvt code errors (-Werror). The code in third_party/ is not included. All CI build jobs use ON, so a change that adds a warning fails CI. All the wvt targets compile with -Wall -Wextra -Wno-unused-parameter.

To add your own compiler flags, use CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS or CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_RELEASE. wvt does not replace them.

WVT_SANITIZE¶

Builds all the programs with compiler sanitizers. Use it to test, not for normal use: the programs are slower and use more memory.

  • address: AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer (-fsanitize=address,undefined). They find out-of-bounds access, use after free, memory leaks (Linux) and undefined behavior. An undefined-behavior error stops the program.

  • thread: ThreadSanitizer (-fsanitize=thread). It finds data races between threads. You cannot use it together with address.

  • Empty (the default): no sanitizers.

The CUDA code (gpu_cuda.cu) does not get the sanitizer flags. Use a separate build folder for each value. Refer to Self-checks.

Output: wvt: sanitizers enabled (address: -fsanitize=address,undefined;...).

WVT_FUZZ¶

ON also builds the libFuzzer targets fuzz_json, fuzz_chain, fuzz_meta and fuzz_parse_si, with AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer. CTest then also runs each target on its seed inputs. The option needs clang: with another compiler, the configure step stops with an error. On macOS, use the clang of the Homebrew llvm package, because Apple clang has no libFuzzer. Refer to Fuzz tests.

Output: wvt: libFuzzer targets enabled (fuzz_json, fuzz_chain, fuzz_meta, fuzz_parse_si).

The CPU FFT¶

The CPU FFT is not an option. On macOS, the build always links the Accelerate framework and uses its vDSP FFT. On Linux, wvt uses its own radix-2 FFT.

Examples¶

A Linux build with the two device backends, and the configure step stops if one is missing:

cmake -S . -B build -DWVT_WITH_RTLSDR=ON -DWVT_WITH_UHD=ON

A minimum build: the file viewer, the simulator and the signal generator file output only:

cmake -S . -B build -DWVT_WITH_RTLSDR=OFF -DWVT_WITH_UHD=OFF -DWVT_WITH_AUDIO=OFF \
      -DWVT_WITH_CUDA=OFF -DWVT_WITH_METAL=OFF

A CUDA build for one GPU type, with shared CUDA libraries:

cmake -S . -B build -DWVT_WITH_CUDA=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=89 -DWVT_CUDA_STATIC=OFF

A build for ThreadSanitizer, in a separate folder:

cmake -S . -B build-tsan -DWVT_SANITIZE=thread -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo

A debug build:

cmake -S . -B build-debug -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug

Build targets¶

cmake --build build makes all these programs. To make one program only, add --target NAME.

Target

Contents

wvt

The application

iqgen

Writes a synthetic test recording

siggen_check

Self-check for the signal generator

audio_check

Self-check for the audio demodulator

log_check

Self-check for the logger

segment_check

Self-check for the time segment rules

extract_check

Self-check for the region export

snapshot_check

Self-check for the plot snapshots

device_check

Self-check for the device list and the sample rate rules

bb_check

Self-check for the BB60 backend, with the simulated device. Only with WVT_BB_SIM=ON

skiq_check

Self-check for the Sidekiq logic. With WVT_SKIQ_SIM=ON, also for the backend with the simulated card

gpu_check

Compares the GPU results with the CPU results, and measures the speed

fuzz_json, fuzz_chain, fuzz_meta, fuzz_parse_si

The fuzz targets. Only with WVT_FUZZ=ON

ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure runs all the self-checks.

For the self-checks, refer to Self-checks and test signals.

Version information¶

At each build, CMake reads two values from git:

  • Build: the short commit hash, for example 523ac6c. If tracked files have changes that are not committed, -dirty is added. Outside a git checkout (for example, a source archive), the value is unknown.

  • Version: the version tag on that commit, for example v1.1. If the commit has no tag, the value is blank.

Help > About wvt shows the two values. wvt also writes them to the start of each log file. You do not have to configure again after a commit or a new tag: the next build updates the values.

Build the documentation¶

The documentation uses Sphinx with the MyST Markdown parser. To make the HTML pages:

pip install -r docs/requirements.txt
sphinx-build -W -b html docs build/docs

Open build/docs/index.html in a browser. The -W option makes each warning an error. CI uses the same command. For the writing rules, refer to Writing the documentation.
